mainTopic: When the עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden for benefit, and whether an אשם תלוי can be brought as a voluntary gift
overview: The amud opens with a question: from when is the עגלה ערופה forbidden for any benefit? Is it forbidden while still alive, or only after its neck is broken? רב המנונא proves it is forbidden while alive. In a משנה about אותו ואת בנו, רבי שמעון exempts someone who slaughters an עגלה ערופה. רבא tries to defend the opposite view, but רב המנונא's proof holds. רבא then brings his own proof from a משנה which says the עגלה is buried because it already 'atoned for its doubt.' That fits only if it becomes forbidden at the עריפה. The גמרא concludes that this is a dispute between תנאים, since a ברייתא holds it is forbidden while alive. A new משנה follows. רבי אליעזר allows a voluntary אשם תלוי, and the חכמים do not. It also teaches when יום כיפור cancels an owed offering. The גמרא explains both sides of the אשם תלוי dispute. The amud ends as רבי חייא begins reciting a teaching before רבא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי ינאי forgot the exact point; his colleagues say going down to the stream forbids it
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי heard a ruling about when the עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden but forgot it. His colleagues leaned toward saying it becomes forbidden once it is brought down to the נחל איתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: I heard a rule about the point at which it becomes forbidden, but I forgot it. The colleagues were inclined to say: its going down to the rough stream is what makes it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי admits he forgot the exact moment the עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden. His colleagues suggest it is the moment the animal is brought down to the valley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the prohibition begins only after the neck is broken (עריפה), or earlier while the animal is still alive. The colleagues pick an earlier point, the going down to the נחל איתן. That means the animal is already forbidden while alive.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
Boundary; here, the point at which the animal becomes forbidden
A rough or hard stream-valley where the calf's neck is broken
Makes it forbidden
The colleagues, the group of scholars

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
I heard a boundary regarding it, but I forgot it,
phrases.notes: The "boundary" is the exact moment the עגלה becomes forbidden for any benefit.

phrases.english: and the colleagues were inclined to say:
its going down to the rough stream is what forbids it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: גְּבוּל שָׁמַעְתִּי בָּהּ וְשָׁכַחְתִּי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden once it is brought down to the נחל איתן, while still alive, and not only after עריפה.

steps.title: רב המנונא brings a משנה to prove it is forbidden while alive
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא asks where his view comes from and quotes a משנה. In it, רבי שמעון exempts and the חכמים obligate someone who slaughters a פרת חטאת, a שור הנסקל, or an עגלה ערופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: From where do I say this? From what we learned in a משנה: One who slaughters a פרת חטאת, a שור הנסקל, or an עגלה ערופה: רבי שמעון exempts him, and the חכמים hold him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא sets up a proof that the עגלה ערופה is forbidden while still alive. In this step he only quotes the source; he explains it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three animals in the משנה are forbidden for benefit. The case is slaughtering one of them on the same day as its mother or offspring (אותו ואת בנו). רבי שמעון and the חכמים disagree on whether he gets punished.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (an opening that introduces a proof)
The red heifer used for purification
An ox sentenced to stoning for killing a person
Exempts from punishment
Hold liable

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: He means: how do I know the עגלה is already forbidden while it is still alive?

phrases.english: For we learned in a mishnah:
One who slaughters a red heifer,
or an ox to be stoned, or a heifer whose neck is broken —
Rabbi Shimon exempts, and the Sages hold him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports the colleagues' view that the animal is forbidden while alive.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the עגלה ערופה is forbidden while still alive
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in חולין about slaughtering a פרת חטאת, a שור הנסקל, and an עגלה ערופה under the laws of אותו ואת בנו

steps.title: According to Rav Hamnuna, the mishnah's argument makes sense
steps.stepSummary: If the animal is forbidden while alive, the slaughter cannot make it fit to eat. The dispute is then simple: רבי שמעון says an unfit slaughter is not counted as slaughter, and the רבנן say it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to me, since I say it is forbidden from when it is alive. Then this is what רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about. רבי שמעון holds: a slaughter that does not make the animal fit is not called slaughter. The רבנן say: a slaughter that does not make the animal fit is still called slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא shows that his view gives a clear reason for the argument in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the עגלה is already forbidden before it is slaughtered, slaughtering it does not make it fit to eat. רבי שמעון says such a slaughter does not count, so there is no אותו ואת בנו and no punishment. The רבנן say it still counts, so he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine, it works well (sets up a contrast with an option that does not work)
From when it is alive
A slaughter that does not make the animal fit to eat
It is called (counts as) slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the animal cannot be eaten. They argue only about whether a slaughter that does not permit the meat still counts as slaughter for the איסור of אותו ואת בנו.

phrases.english: It works well according to me,
since I say it is forbidden from when it is alive;
in this Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis disagree,
for Rabbi Shimon holds:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה – לֹא שְׁמָהּ שְׁחִיטָה.
phrases.english: a slaughter that does not make it fit is not called slaughter.
And the Rabbis say:
a slaughter that does not make it fit is called slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְדִידִי, דְּאָמֵינָא מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quoted משנה fits his view.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the עגלה ערופה is forbidden while alive
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן over whether שחיטה שאינה ראויה counts as slaughter

steps.title: If it were forbidden only after the neck-breaking, רבי שמעון's exemption makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: If the עגלה is forbidden only after עריפה, then slaughtering it earlier does make it fit to eat. So why would רבי שמעון exempt him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say it becomes forbidden only after the neck is broken, why does רבי שמעון exempt him? It is a slaughter that makes the animal fit!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא finishes his proof by challenging the other view, that the prohibition starts only after עריפה. Under that view, רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה cannot be explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the other view, an עגלה slaughtered before its neck is broken was never forbidden. The slaughter would make it fit to eat, so even רבי שמעון should agree that it counts and he is liable. Since רבי שמעון exempts, the עגלה must already be forbidden while alive.

keyTerms.meaning: After the breaking of the neck
Why?
A slaughter that makes the animal fit to eat

steps.whatToRemember: רב המנונא proves from רבי שמעון's exemption that the עגלה ערופה is already forbidden while alive. Otherwise slaughtering it would be a fit slaughter, and even רבי שמעון would hold him liable.

phrases.english: But if you say it is forbidden only after the neck-breaking,
why does Rabbi Shimon exempt?
It is a slaughter that makes it fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לְאַחַר עֲרִיפָה, אַמַּאי פָּטַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the בשלמא: the other view cannot explain רבי שמעון's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the עגלה ערופה becomes forbidden only after עריפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view, slaughter before עריפה makes the animal fit to eat, so רבי שמעון would have no reason to exempt.

steps.title: Suggested answer: רבי שמעון holds slaughter is a valid way to do the עגלה
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא raises a possible answer to his own question from Step 4: perhaps רבי שמעון holds that slaughtering the עגלה counts as its proper ritual. If so, the slaughter itself makes the animal forbidden, so it never becomes fit to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: רבי שמעון holds that an עגלה done by slaughter is valid...
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא raises a possible way to explain רבי שמעון even if the עגלה becomes forbidden only at the end. He is about to reject this suggestion himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 the problem was this: if the עגלה is not forbidden while alive, slaughter makes it fit to eat, so why would רבי שמעון exempt? The answer is that for רבי שמעון, slaughter counts as the עגלה's ritual itself. So the slaughter makes it forbidden, and it is an unfit slaughter after all.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a suggested answer
Ritual slaughter by cutting the throat
Valid, done the proper way

phrases.english: And if you would say: Rabbi Shimon holds
a heifer killed by slaughter is valid,
phrases.notes: He means slaughter counts as doing the עגלה's ritual, so the slaughter itself makes it forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: סָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עֶגְלָה בִּשְׁחִיטָה כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the קשיא of Step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets רבי שמעון's view about the method of the עגלה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Slaughter would make a not-yet-forbidden עגלה fit to eat, so רבי שמעון should obligate.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון slaughter is a valid עריפה, so it forbids the animal and is an unfit slaughter.

steps.title: A משנה says slaughter is invalid for the עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that what is valid for the פרה is invalid for the עגלה, and the reverse. A פרה is valid with slaughter, while an עגלה is valid only with עריפה. So slaughter is invalid for the עגלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: what is valid for the פרה is invalid for the עגלה ערופה, and what is invalid for the פרה is valid for the עגלה ערופה. The פרה is valid with slaughter and invalid with עריפה. The עגלה is valid with עריפה and invalid with slaughter!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא rejects the suggestion of Step 5 by quoting a משנה that says slaughter does not work for an עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion needed slaughter to count as a valid ritual for the עגלה. The משנה says plainly that an עגלה killed by slaughter is invalid. So the slaughter does not forbid the animal, and the question of Step 4 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer (פרה אדומה), whose ashes purify
Breaking the neck from behind
Invalid, unfit

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
What is valid for the red heifer is invalid for the heifer whose neck is broken;
what is invalid for the red heifer is valid for the heifer whose neck is broken.
The red heifer is valid with slaughter and invalid with breaking the neck;
the heifer is valid with breaking the neck and invalid with slaughter!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: כָּשֵׁר בַּפָּרָה פָּסוּל בְּעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer of Step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that slaughter is valid for the עגלה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A משנה states that slaughter is invalid for the עגלה ערופה

steps.title: רבא's later answer: רבי שמעון disagrees with that משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא had no answer in the moment and stayed quiet. After רב המנונא left, רבא said he could have answered that רבי שמעון disagrees with the משנה and holds that slaughter is valid for the עגלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent. After רב המנונא left, רבא said: Why didn't I tell him that רבי שמעון holds that an עגלה done by slaughter is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא, who holds the עגלה is forbidden only after עריפה, could not answer at first. Later he realized he could have said the משנה is not the view of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה from Step 6 only shows what the author of that משנה holds. רבא says רבי שמעון may simply disagree with it. Then the suggestion of Step 5 works for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent: had no answer at that moment
After he left
Why? What is the reason?

phrases.english: He was silent.
phrases.notes: This is רבא, the one who holds the עגלה becomes forbidden only after עריפה.

phrases.english: After he left, he said:
phrases.notes: After רב המנונא left, רבא spoke.

phrases.english: Why didn't I say to him
that Rabbi Shimon holds:
a heifer killed by slaughter is valid!
phrases.notes: He means רבי שמעון simply disagrees with the משנה just quoted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתִּיק. לְבָתַר דִּנְפַק, אֲמַר: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמֵינָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the opposing משנה to other תנאים, not רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה rules out slaughter for the עגלה for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון disagrees with the משנה and holds that slaughter is valid.

steps.title: רב המנונא's reply: no תנא holds that view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב המנונא would answer that if some תנא held that slaughter is valid for the עגלה, it would appear somewhere. Since no source says it, you cannot invent it for רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב המנונא would tell you: no תנא would have been left out who teaches us that an עגלה done by slaughter is valid, so that you could say it is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's later answer from Step 7, explaining what רב המנונא would have replied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer needs a תנא who holds that slaughter works for the עגלה. We never find such a view taught anywhere. So there is no basis to say רבי שמעון holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: No תנא would have left it out: if the view existed, it would be taught somewhere
A sage of the משנה era

phrases.english: But Rav Hamnuna would say to you:
No tanna would have been left out
phrases.notes: Literally, no תנא would have slipped away. If such a view existed, someone would have taught it.

phrases.english: who teaches us that a heifer killed by slaughter is valid,
so that you could say it is Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר לָךְ: לָא נִשְׁתְּמִיט תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's later answer from Step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects attributing to רבי שמעון the view that slaughter is valid
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No source anywhere records a תנא who holds that slaughter is valid for the עגלה
steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to explain רבי שמעון's exemption according to רבא fails. רב המנונא's proof from that משנה still stands.

steps.title: רבא's own source: before עריפה the עגלה goes back to the flock
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה: unlike the case before it, if the killer is found before the עגלה's neck is broken, it goes out and grazes with the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I say it? From what we learned: an עגלה ערופה is not like that. Before its neck is broken, it goes out and grazes with the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now opens his own proof that the עגלה becomes forbidden only after עריפה. He quotes the משנה his proof is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that before עריפה, the עגלה can go back to ordinary life with the flock. That suggests it never became holy or forbidden while alive. The next step spells out the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? Introduces the speaker's own source
It goes out and grazes with the flock: goes back to being an ordinary animal

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
From what we learned: a heifer whose neck is broken is not so;
before its neck was broken,
it goes out and grazes among the flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? מִדִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending against רב המנונא fails, רבא brings proof for his own view
steps.raayaObject: The עגלה becomes forbidden only after עריפה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: if the killer is found before עריפה, the עגלה goes out and grazes with the flock

steps.title: If it were forbidden while alive, it could not return to the flock
steps.stepSummary: רבא draws the inference: if the עגלה were forbidden while still alive, it could not go back to graze like a normal animal. So it must become forbidden only at the עריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is forbidden from when it is alive, why does it go out and graze with the flock? It already became forbidden while alive!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his proof by showing that the משנה does not fit the view that the עגלה is forbidden while alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A forbidden animal cannot simply go back to ordinary use. Since the משנה lets the עגלה return to the flock before עריפה, it was not forbidden yet. This supports רבא against the colleagues of Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: From when it is alive, before it is killed
It became forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof: the משנה lets the עגלה go back to the flock before עריפה, so it is forbidden only after עריפה.

phrases.english: And if you say it is forbidden from when it is alive,
why does it go out and graze among the flock?
It was already forbidden from when it was alive!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מֵחַיִּים, אַמַּאי תֵּצֵא וְתִרְעֶה בָּעֵדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the inference from the משנה quoted in Step 9
steps.raayaObject: The prohibition of the עגלה begins only at עריפה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Returning to the flock is impossible for an animal already forbidden while alive

steps.title: Rereading the משנה: before it was ready for breaking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof by changing how we read the משנה. It now says 'before it was ready to have its neck broken.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Read the משנה this way: if the killer is found before the עגלה was ready to have its neck broken, it goes back to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's proof by rereading the משנה. Now it is talking about an earlier moment: before the עגלה was even ready for the עריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the עגלה can go back to graze, so it must not be forbidden while alive. The answer is that the משנה only means it can graze if the killer is found before the עגלה reaches the point of being ready for breaking. From that point on, it could already be forbidden while still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking the neck of the עגלה
Ready / fit to have its neck broken

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say the עגלה is never forbidden while alive. It moves the cutoff point earlier, to when the עגלה is ready for breaking.

phrases.english: Teach: before it was fit for having its neck broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנִי: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאֵית לַעֲרִיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's inference from step 10 by rereading the משנה from step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's proof that the עגלה becomes forbidden only at the עריפה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as talking about a time before the עגלה was ready for breaking. That leaves room for it to become forbidden while still alive.

steps.title: The next line says 'after its neck was broken'
steps.stepSummary: רבא points to the next line of the משנה. It says that if the killer is found after the neck was broken, the עגלה is buried. That suggests the breaking is what makes it forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the next line: if the killer is found after its neck was broken, it is buried where it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the new reading by pointing to the second half of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next line ties burial to the moment the neck was broken. That suggests the עגלה becomes forbidden at the breaking, not before. So the rereading in step 11 seems not to match the משנה's own wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a משנה or ברייתא
It must be buried where it is

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
after its neck was broken, it shall be buried in its place!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: מִשֶּׁנֶּעֶרְפָה – תִּקָּבֵר בִּמְקוֹמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rereading offered in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rereading that the cutoff is when the עגלה is 'ready for breaking'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second half of the משנה names the actual breaking as the turning point. That suggests the עגלה becomes forbidden only then.

steps.title: Rereading the second line the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the second line in the same way. It means 'after it was ready for breaking,' not 'after it was broken.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Read that line too as: after it was ready to have its neck broken, it is buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא handles רבא's new challenge with the same trick it used before. It rereads the second line too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both lines speak about the moment the עגלה is ready for breaking, the משנה stays consistent. On this reading, the עגלה could be forbidden from that point, while it is still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: From when it was fit / ready

phrases.english: Teach: after it was fit for having its neck broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנִי: מִשֶּׁנִּרְאֵית לַעֲרִיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 using the same rereading method as step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא makes the actual breaking the turning point.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא also means the moment the עגלה became ready for breaking.

steps.title: The last line: it already atoned for the doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the משנה's own reason: the עגלה comes for a doubt, and it has already atoned for that doubt. That only works if its neck was really broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the משנה: because it came for a doubt from the start, it atoned for its doubt and it's done. But if we are talking about while it is alive, it has not atoned yet!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a stronger challenge from the end of the משנה, which explains why the עגלה is buried. This reason cannot be reread away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the עגלה 'atoned for its doubt.' Atonement only happens through the actual עריפה. A living עגלה that is merely 'ready' has not atoned for anything yet. So the משנה must be talking about a real broken neck. That means the עגלה becomes forbidden at the עריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: For a situation of doubt (here, the unknown killer)
It atoned for its doubt
While still alive

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
that from the outset it comes for a doubt,
it atoned for its doubt, and that is done.
But if it is while it is alive,
it has still not atoned for its doubt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: שֶׁעַל הַסָּפֵק בָּאָה מִתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the rereading from step 13 does not fit the משנה's own stated reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rereading that the משנה is talking about a living עגלה that is only 'ready for breaking'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Atonement only happens through the actual breaking. A משנה that says 'it atoned' must be talking about an עגלה that was really broken.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge works, so the גמרא stops rereading the משנה and turns to a different answer.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the משנה holds the עגלה becomes forbidden at the עריפה. It answers that this is a dispute between תנאים, and it starts quoting a ברייתא on רב המנונא's side.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a dispute between תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: the תורה speaks of sacrifices that make a person ready and sacrifices that atone inside the מקדש, and also of ones that make a person ready and ones that atone outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on rereading the משנה. Instead it says other תנאים disagree, and it begins quoting a ברייתא that sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה really does hold the עגלה becomes forbidden at the עריפה. But רב המנונא is not left without a source: another תנא holds it is forbidden while alive. The ברייתא first lists two groups of sacrifices, inside and outside, so it can compare them in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
A sacrifice that makes a person ready / permitted, for example to eat holy food
A sacrifice that brings atonement
Inside the מקדש / outside the מקדש

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים, as it is taught:
It is stated: one that makes ready and one that atones, inside,
and it is stated: one that makes ready and one that atones, outside.
phrases.notes: The 'outside' atoning one is the עגלה ערופה, which is not done in the מקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 14 about the משנה and answers instead by pointing to a תנא who disagrees.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that no one holds the עגלה is forbidden while alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is one view. A ברייתא holds the other view.

steps.title: Outside sacrifices are compared to inside ones
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its comparison. Inside the מקדש, the תורה treats the one that makes ready like the one that atones. The same is true outside. This supports the view that the עגלה is forbidden while alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as with the ones inside, the תורה made the one that makes ready like the one that atones, so too with the ones outside, it made the one that makes ready like the one that atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא completes its comparison. This gives רב המנונא a תנא who supports his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns the outside offerings from the inside ones. Inside, the תורה treats the מכשיר like the מכפר, so outside the מכשיר (the birds of the מצורע) is also treated like the מכפר, which is the עגלה ערופה. On this view the עגלה is forbidden while still alive, so רב המנונא has a תנא on his side, even though the משנה רבא quoted in step 9 disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה treated the one that makes ready like the one that atones
That is stated / mentioned

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה holds that the עגלה becomes forbidden only at the עריפה. A ברייתא holds that it is forbidden while still alive, so the question is a dispute between תנאים.

phrases.english: Just as the one that makes ready and the one that atones stated inside,
it made, with them, the one that makes ready like the one that atones –
so too the one that makes ready and the one that atones stated outside,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: it made the one that makes ready like the one that atones.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה מַכְשִׁיר וּמְכַפֵּר הָאָמוּר בִּפְנִים, עָשָׂה בּוֹ מַכְשִׁיר כִּמְכַפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 15 and draws its comparison.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the עגלה ערופה is forbidden while still alive.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that compares the outside מכשיר and מכפר to the inside ones.
steps.whyThisMatters: It answers the challenge from the משנה in step 14. The משנה does hold that the עגלה becomes forbidden only at the עריפה, but רב המנונא still has a תנא on his side: this ברייתא holds it is forbidden while alive.

steps.title: A person may volunteer an אשם תלוי any day
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that a person may bring an אשם תלוי as a voluntary offering whenever he wants. It was called the 'אשם of the pious.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי אליעזר says: A person may volunteer an אשם תלוי every day and at any time he wants. It was called 'the אשם of the pious.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי אליעזר says you do not need a real doubt to bring an אשם תלוי. You can bring it as a gift any time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an אשם תלוי comes when a person is unsure whether he sinned. רבי אליעזר allows it even with no specific doubt. Pious people brought it because they always worried they might have sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A 'suspended' guilt offering, brought when unsure whether one sinned
Brings voluntarily, as a gift
'The אשם of the pious', the nickname for this voluntary offering

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A person may volunteer a provisional guilt offering
every day and at any time that he wants.
It was called the guilt offering of the pious.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִתְנַדֵּב אָדָם אָשָׁם תָּלוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, an אשם תלוי may be brought voluntarily at any time.

steps.title: בבא בן בוטא brought one every day except after יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells that בבא בן בוטא brought a voluntary אשם תלוי every day except the day after יום כיפור. He swore he would have brought it then too, but he was told to wait until he had a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about בבא בן בוטא that he brought a voluntary אשם תלוי every day, except for one day, the day after יום כיפור. He said: 'By this Temple! If they let me, I would bring it. But they tell me: Wait until you come into a doubt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a real-life example of a pious man who did what רבי אליעזר describes. It also shows the one day he could not do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום כיפור had just wiped away any possible doubts, so the day after it there was clearly no doubt yet. The people in charge told him to wait until a doubt could have come up. So even on this approach, the offering needs at least some time in which a doubt could exist.

keyTerms.meaning: 'By this dwelling', an oath by the בית המקדש
A doubt or uncertainty
Wait

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בבא בן בוטא skipped that day by choice. He wanted to bring it, but they did not allow him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל בָּבָא בֶּן בּוּטָא
phrases.english: They said about Bava ben Buta

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה מִתְנַדֵּב אָשָׁם תָּלוּי בְּכׇל יוֹם,
phrases.english: that he would volunteer a provisional guilt offering every day,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מֵאַחַר יוֹם כִּיפּוּרִים יוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: except for one day, the day after Yom Kippur.
He said: By this abode!
phrases.notes: He is swearing by the Temple, where the שכינה rests.

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין לִי הָיִיתִי מֵבִיא,
phrases.english: If they had let me, I would have brought it,
but they say to me:
Wait until you enter into a doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל בָּבָא בֶּן בּוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a real case of the voluntary אשם that רבי אליעזר allows.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view that an אשם תלוי can be brought voluntarily.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of בבא בן בוטא.

steps.title: חכמים: only for a doubt about a כרת sin
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר. An אשם תלוי is brought only for a doubt about a sin that carries כרת if done on purpose and a חטאת if done by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: One brings an אשם תלוי only for a sin whose deliberate violation brings כרת and whose accidental violation brings a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר and say no voluntary אשם תלוי is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, an אשם תלוי is not a free gift. It needs a real doubt, and the doubt must be about the kind of sin that would require a חטאת if he knew for sure he had done it by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing it on purpose carries the punishment of כרת
Doing it by mistake requires a חטאת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: an אשם תלוי can be a voluntary gift. חכמים: it is only for a real doubt about a כרת-level sin.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
One does not bring a provisional guilt offering
except for something whose intentional violation is punished by karet
and whose unwitting violation requires a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם תלוי is brought only for a doubt about a sin of כרת that would require a חטאת if done by mistake.

steps.title: יום כיפור cancels an owed אשם תלוי but not definite offerings
steps.stepSummary: People who owe definite חטאות or אשמות must still bring them after יום כיפור. People who owe an אשם תלוי are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those who owe sin offerings or definite guilt offerings, and יום כיפור passed, must bring them after יום כיפור. Those who owe provisional guilt offerings are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new rule: what יום כיפור does to offerings a person still owes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום כיפור atones for doubtful sins, so the אשם תלוי, which only covers a doubt, is no longer needed. A definite sin still requires its own offering even after יום כיפור.

keyTerms.meaning: Definite, for a sin known for sure
Sin offerings
Exempt

phrases.english: Those liable to bring sin offerings and definite guilt offerings
for whom Yom Kippur has passed
are liable to bring them after Yom Kippur,
but those liable to bring provisional guilt offerings are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיבֵי חַטָּאוֹת וַאֲשָׁמוֹת וַדָּאִין שֶׁעָבַר עֲלֵיהֶן יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within the משנה: the effect of יום כיפור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Definite offerings must still be brought after יום כיפור, but an owed אשם תלוי is cancelled.

steps.title: A doubtful sin on יום כיפור itself is covered
steps.stepSummary: If a person comes into a doubtful sin on יום כיפור, even right before nightfall, he is exempt from an אשם תלוי. The whole day atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who came into a doubtful sin on יום כיפור, even at nightfall, is exempt, because the entire day atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that even a doubt that comes up during יום כיפור itself is atoned by the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think only doubts from before יום כיפור are covered. The משנה teaches that every part of the day atones, up to its very end.

keyTerms.meaning: Nightfall, the end of the day
Atones

phrases.english: One who came into
an uncertain sin on Yom Kippur,
even at nightfall, is exempt,
as the entire day atones.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁבָּא בְּיָדוֹ סְפֵק עֲבֵירָה בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule about יום כיפור to doubts that arise on the day itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubtful sin on יום כיפור, even at its very end, is atoned, so no אשם תלוי is needed.

steps.title: A woman's doubtful bird חטאת is still brought after יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: A woman who owes a bird חטאת because of a doubt must still bring it after יום כיפור, because it permits her to eat קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who owes a doubtful bird sin offering, and יום כיפור passed, must bring it after יום כיפור, because it makes her fit to eat sacrificial meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives an exception. This doubtful offering is not cancelled by יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other doubtful offerings are cancelled because יום כיפור atones for the doubt. Her bird offering is mainly not about atonement. It completes her purification so she may eat קדשים, and יום כיפור cannot do that for her.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird sin offering
Makes fit or eligible
Sacrificial meat

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether יום כיפור cancels an offering depends on what the offering is for. Atonement offerings are cancelled, but offerings that make a person fit are not.

phrases.aramaic: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ חַטַּאת הָעוֹף סָפֵק,
phrases.english: A woman who has a doubtful bird sin offering upon her,
and Yom Kippur has passed for her
is liable to bring it after Yom Kippur,
because it makes her eligible to eat sacrificial meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ חַטַּאת הָעוֹף סָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the rule that יום כיפור cancels doubtful offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman's doubtful bird חטאת must still be brought after יום כיפור, since its purpose is to make her fit to eat קדשים.

steps.title: If the doubt is cleared after מליקה, the bird is buried
steps.stepSummary: If a doubtful bird חטאת already had its neck pinched and then it became known that it was not needed, the bird must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bird sin offering brought because of a doubt: if it became known after its neck was pinched, it must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a rule about a doubtful bird offering when the doubt is cleared up too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the מליקה is done, the bird is already a קרבן and is forbidden to benefit from. So even though it turns out she did not need it, it cannot be used and must be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: Its neck was pinched (מליקה), the way bird offerings are killed
It became known
It must be buried

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's main points: רבי אליעזר allows a voluntary אשם תלוי and חכמים do not. יום כיפור cancels doubtful offerings but not definite ones, and not the woman's bird offering. A doubtful bird חטאת found to be unneeded after מליקה is buried.

phrases.english: A bird sin offering that is brought because of a doubt,
if it became known after it was pinched, it must be buried.
phrases.notes: What became known is that she was not obligated after all.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטַּאת הָעוֹף הַבָּאָה עַל הַסָּפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the doubtful bird חטאת with the case where the doubt is resolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubtful bird חטאת that turns out to be unneeded after מליקה must be buried.

steps.title: What is רבי אליעזר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why רבי אליעזר holds that a person may bring an אשם תלוי as a voluntary offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking for the source of רבי אליעזר's view. This sets up the next step, where his reasoning is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר said a person may bring an אשם תלוי any day he wants, even without a specific doubt. That sounds strange, because an אשם is normally a required offering. So the גמרא wants to know what pushed him to say this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's dispute about a voluntary אשם תלוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's view that an אשם תלוי can be brought voluntarily.

steps.title: The later חטאת shows the אשם תלוי was only a gift
steps.stepSummary: If the אשם תלוי were a true obligation, it should exempt him from a חטאת once he finds out he sinned. Since he still brings a חטאת, the אשם תלוי must be a voluntary gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think it is an obligation, why does he bring a חטאת when he finds out he sinned? So we learn that it is a gift offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's logic. He proves from the later חטאת that the אשם תלוי was never a real obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law is that a person who brought an אשם תלוי and later learns he really sinned must still bring a חטאת. If the אשם תלוי had been a real required offering, it should have covered him. Since it doesn't, רבי אליעזר concludes it is basically a voluntary offering, so anyone may bring it whenever he wants.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you were to think)
An obligation; a required offering
A voluntary gift offering
Learn from this; we can conclude

phrases.english: If it enters your mind that it is an obligation,
[when] it becomes known to him that he sinned,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording of the text.

phrases.english: why does he bring a sin offering?
Rather, learn from this: it is a gift offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ חוֹבָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 by giving רבי אליעזר's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because a חטאת is still required after the sin becomes known, the אשם תלוי did not fulfill an obligation, so it must be a נדבה.

steps.title: The חכמים: only עולה and שלמים can be gifts
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים respond that only עולה and שלמים come as vows and gifts. חטאת and אשם are always obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: עולה and שלמים come as vows and gifts, but חטאת and אשם are obligations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the חכמים's response to רבי אליעזר. They set a basic rule about which offerings can ever be voluntary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים divide the offerings into two groups. עולה and שלמים can be brought as a gift or a vow. חטאת and every kind of אשם, including the אשם תלוי, are only brought when a person is required to bring them.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the altar
A peace offering, shared by the altar, the כהנים and the owner
A vow and a gift, the two kinds of voluntary offerings

phrases.english: And the Rabbis would say:
It is a burnt offering and a peace offering that come
as a vow and a gift offering,
but a sin offering and a guilt offering are obligations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן: עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים הוּא דְּאָתוּ בְּנֶדֶר וּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the חכמים's opposing view in response to רבי אליעזר's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Category rule: only certain offerings can ever be voluntary.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the אשם תלוי doesn't exempt from a later חטאת, it must be a gift.
steps.terutzMaskana: An אשם, including an אשם תלוי, belongs to the category of required offerings, never gifts.

steps.title: The אשם תלוי protects the person until he finds out
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים explain that the אשם תלוי is brought before the person knows about his sin in order to protect him. The תורה had pity on the bodies of the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he brings an אשם תלוי before he finds out is to protect him, because the תורה had pity on the bodies of the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים now answer רבי אליעזר's proof directly. They explain why the אשם תלוי can be a real obligation even though a חטאת still comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר argued that if the person still owes a חטאת later, the אשם תלוי must have been a gift. The חכמים say the אשם תלוי was never meant to bring full atonement. It is a required protection for the time of doubt, so the later חטאת does not prove it was voluntary.

keyTerms.meaning: To protect him
The תורה had pity

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the אשם תלוי is a 'half' חטאת that gets finished later. According to the חכמים it has a different job: it protects the person while he doesn't know. Atonement for the actual sin comes from the חטאת.

phrases.english: And as for a provisional guilt offering, this is the reason
that he brings it before it becomes known to him:
to protect him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל גּוּפָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: as the Torah had pity on the bodies of the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָשָׁם תָּלוּי, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּמַיְיתֵי מִקַּמֵּי דְּמִתְיְידַע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the חכמים's answer by rejecting רבי אליעזר's proof from the later חטאת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the offering: it protects, it does not fully atone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because a later חטאת is required, the אשם תלוי accomplished nothing required, so it must be a gift.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אשם תלוי is a required protection for the time of doubt, so a later חטאת is still needed for the sin itself.

steps.title: Maybe the אשם תלוי can come both ways, like עולה and שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי: עולה and שלמים come both as obligations and as gifts. Why can't the אשם תלוי also be both?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרבא said to רב אשי: Perhaps the אשם תלוי is like עולה and שלמים. They come both as obligations and as gifts, so the אשם תלוי should come as an obligation and also as a gift!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges the חכמים's neat split between required offerings and gift offerings. He suggests that the אשם תלוי might come both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים put עולה and שלמים in the gift group. Yet those offerings are sometimes required too, so one offering can belong to both groups. So the fact that the אשם תלוי is sometimes required does not prove it can never be a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; maybe
Just as ... so too (a comparison)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
Perhaps a provisional guilt offering is like a burnt offering and a peace offering:
just as a burnt offering and a peace offering
come as obligations and come as gift offerings,
so too a provisional guilt offering, which comes as an obligation,
also comes as a gift offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי כְּעוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים's split of offerings into 'gift' and 'obligation' groups.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's claim that an אשם, being an obligation, can never be a gift.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולה and שלמים show that one offering can be both required and voluntary, so the same could be true of the אשם תלוי.

steps.title: Each offering follows its main setting in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the תורה mainly presents עולה and שלמים as gifts. It mainly presents the אשם תלוי as an obligation, so it cannot come as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: עולה and שלמים are mainly written as gifts. The אשם תלוי is mainly written as an obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the חכמים. He explains why the comparison to עולה and שלמים doesn't work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is how the תורה mainly presents each offering. עולה and שלמים appear mainly as gifts, and they are required only in special cases. The אשם תלוי appears mainly as an obligation, like חטאת and אשם, so it has no voluntary form.

keyTerms.meaning: Mainly; the basic setting
It is written (in the תורה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: the אשם תלוי can be a voluntary gift, because a חטאת is still needed later. חכמים: it is always an obligation. It protects the person during his doubt, and the תורה mainly presents it as a required offering, unlike עולה and שלמים.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A burnt offering and a peace offering are primarily written as gift offerings,
a provisional guilt offering is primarily written as an obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים עִיקָּר בִּנְדָבָה כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא בריה דרבא's challenge and upholds the חכמים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on how the תורה mainly presents each offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since עולה and שלמים come both ways, the אשם תלוי could too.
steps.terutzMaskana: An offering's main setting in the תורה defines it. The אשם תלוי's main setting is obligation, so it has no gift form.

steps.title: רבי חייא recites a teaching before רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a teaching that רבי חייא recited in the presence of רבא. The content of the teaching comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא recited a teaching in front of רבא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us who is about to quote a teaching and in front of whom, so get ready for the actual teaching in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is stated yet. The line only names the speaker (רבי חייא) and the listener (רבא). The teaching he recites will bring new material into the discussion of the אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of him; in his presence
A reciter who memorized and repeated earlier teachings in the study hall
A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the ruling in this line. It only introduces who is speaking. The actual teaching comes right after the colon.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught (recited a teaching)
before Rava:

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אשי's answer that the אשם תלוי comes only as an obligation, the גמרא brings in a recited teaching to continue the discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line introduces a teaching recited by רבי חייא before רבא, and its content follows.
